best_for: People who already run a Jellyfin server at home and want a desktop player that plays more files directly, so the server does less transcoding.
description:
Jellyfin Media Player is the desktop app for Jellyfin, a free media server project built entirely by volunteers. The app shows Jellyfin's own interface inside a Qt WebEngine window. Jellyfin does not run servers for its users, and the project says its software has no tracking and does not phone home.

Through the app you browse your movies with their artwork and your shows sorted by season, ready to binge. Play your music and playlists, watch live TV and schedule recordings, and read books and comics. SyncPlay lets you watch a movie in step with friends in other homes.

points.title: It needs a Jellyfin server
points.text: This is a client, not a media server. You point it at a Jellyfin server you or someone else runs. Jellyfin says no subscription is needed for the server or any official client.

points.title: mpv does the playing
points.text: Playback uses libmpv, with hardware decoding and audio passthrough. The README says it plays more formats without transcoding than the web client, which spares a weak server.

points.title: Tweak it with mpv.conf
points.text: You can drop an `mpv.conf` file into the settings folder to tune playback the way mpv users are used to. Settings are kept per profile.

points.title: Now called Jellyfin Desktop
points.text: The GitHub project and the 1.12.0 release are branded jellyfin-desktop. Same app, new name, so look for either when searching.

points.title: Windows needs admin rights
points.text: The 1.12.0 notes say the Windows installer needs administrator rights. PCs with CPUs from before about 2013, or that show error 0xc0000142, should use the x64-legacy build.

points.title: macOS 12 left behind
points.text: The 1.12.0 release notes say this version drops macOS 12 support. Builds exist for both Intel and Apple Silicon Macs.

points.title: Linux is not listed here
points.text: This page covers Windows and macOS. The project ships Linux through Flathub. The Windows listing keeps 12 versions; macOS lists only the current release, so a Mac downgrade needs another source.
